title: Improving mitochondria and ER stability helps eliminate upper motor neuron degeneration that occurs due to mSOD1 toxicity and TDP‐43 pathology
one_line: Using UCHL1-eGFP reporter crosses to visualise diseased upper motor neurons in vivo, the authors show that mSOD1 toxicity and TDP-43 pathology converge on mitochondrial/ER destruction, and that oral NU-9 restores organelle integrity and halts UMN degeneration.
key_claims: Electron microscopy showed loss of mitochondrial cristae, expanded/fractured ER cisternae detached from ribosomes, and apical dendrite vacuolisation in diseased UMNs from both mSOD1 and TDP-43 models, and the same pattern appeared in postmortem human ALS Betz cells.
NU-9, from a >50,000-compound screen in PC12 cells, has 94% oral bioavailability, crosses the blood-brain barrier, no hERG inhibition, and a NOAEL of 100 mg/kg.

Oral gavage NU-9 (20 or 100 mg/kg/day, postnatal day 60 to day 120) raised the proportion of structurally healthy mitochondria in mSOD1 UMNs from ~10% (vehicle) to 86%, reassembled ER cisternae with attached ribosomes, and cleared apical dendrite vacuoles.
Treated disease mice had UMN counts virtually identical to wild-type controls and significantly improved hanging wire test performance; immunocytochemistry showed reduced misfolded SOD1 levels.
An earlier preliminary checkpoint noted 13% lifespan extension in mSOD1 mice at 20 mg/kg, but the core study used cellular rescue rather than survival as its endpoint.
limitations: NU-9 gave no protection to lower motor neurons in the lumbar spinal cord, which degenerated at the same rate as untreated controls.
All efficacy data are from transgenic mouse models; human evidence is limited to postmortem ultrastructural comparison.
Treatment window was fixed (P60–P120) with outcomes assessed at end stage, so durability and later-onset dosing were not tested.
Motor function was assessed by a single behavioural assay (hanging wire test).
Mechanism by which NU-9 stabilises mitochondria and ER is not resolved beyond reduced mSOD1 levels.
open_questions: Does combining NU-9 with a lower-motor-neuron-directed agent preserve the whole motor circuit and extend function?
Would NU-9 rescue UMNs if treatment begins after substantial degeneration, and is the effect sustained beyond day 120?
Does the shared organelle-failure signature make NU-9 useful in other neurodegenerative diseases with ER/mitochondrial collapse?
What is NU-9's direct molecular target that restores cristae and ER cisternae?
